h: Using Houndshill as your Blackpool base
p: Plenty of visitors treat Houndshill as a handy launch pad rather than just a place to shop. Park up in the multi-storey, grab whatever you need for the day, and you're within a few minutes' walk of most of the town centre's big hitters. It's also a sensible regrouping point if your party splits up, because everyone knows where it is.

Timing matters in Blackpool. Summer weekends and the Illuminations season in the autumn bring huge crowds into town, and the roads and car parks fill up quickly. Arriving early in the day makes life a lot easier, especially with kids in tow. On quieter days, it's a pleasant, unhurried place to browse with a coffee in hand.

Step out and the classic Blackpool day is all around you. Inside the Tower, the famous Tower Ballroom is a stunning sight with its ornate ceiling and Wurlitzer organ. Down on the Promenade, look out for the Comedy Carpet, a giant artwork of jokes and catchphrases set into the ground in front of the Tower. The Grand Theatre on Church Street is a beautiful Victorian playhouse, while the trams along the seafront will whisk you north towards North Pier and beyond, or south towards the Pleasure Beach. And of course the Golden Mile's amusement arcades, with their flashing lights and coin pushers, are just a short walk away, part of the fun of any proper Blackpool trip. Just remember that some arcade areas are 18+ only.
